meta.title: Oopswhere
meta.description: Your USOS timetable, finally readable. Sign in once, through your university. No database, no passwords.

clash.label: Overlapping classes

clash.body: We show both. We can't put you in two rooms at once, but at least the timetable won't pretend everything is fine.

phone.label: On the move
phone.title: Your phone isn't a microscope.
phone.body: Check your next class on the move, without zooming in like you're examining a specimen.

landing.promiseLead: We don't add another account to your collection. Your password stays on your university's site.
promise: You enter your password only on your university's site. We never see it.
A student database? We don't have one.
Your class-group list lives in an encrypted cookie on your device. We have no account database.
After sign-in, we can show your schedule without using your account again. Refresh groups when they change.
landing.faqTitle: Yes, we saw that question coming.
landing.faqLead: No need to ask the group chat. This time.
faq: Is this the university's official site?
No. We don't have a stamp; we use USOS, and sign-in happens on your university's official site.
Yes. Current and upcoming classes come with a time and room. Right next to the name, just to make things easy. Kidding.
What if USOS has a bad day?
We'll show the last timetable we fetched and warn you it may be out of date. USOS has Mondays too.
Can I refresh my class groups?
Yes. Use the account menu to refresh groups if you switch during the term. Your timetable can move on.
Nothing. Your time already costs enough. The code is open, and you can report bugs on GitHub.
landing.closingBody: See what's on, what's next, and where. Save your energy for running between buildings.

privacy.title: Privacy
intro: Oopswhere has no database and never sees your password. You sign in on your university's own site (USOS), and we receive one-time access that we use only to read your list of class groups and your first name. We revoke that access right away.
Oopswhere is an independent open-source project. It is not run by or affiliated with ZUT.

data.title: Your data
body: The group list and first name are stored in an encrypted cookie in your browser. The server keeps nothing about you. Signing out deletes the cookie.
Class group timetables, lecturer names and rooms are public USOS data. We fetch them from USOS anonymously and cache them briefly so we don't put load on the university's servers.

Legal basis: we process your groups and first name because we can't show you the timetable you ask for without them (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR). Providing them is voluntary, but without signing in the app can't show your timetable. We show lecturer names as part of the public timetable, in our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

analytics.title: Analytics
body: Our server counts login results (successful, cancelled, failed) and how fast the timetable loads. These counts go to PostHog (EU servers) without your IP address or anything else that could identify you.

Only if you agree, the app also measures in your browser: page views, calendar actions such as changing the week, app errors and page speed, along with the browser and device type and an approximate location (country, city) worked out from your IP address. This also goes to PostHog. PostHog sets no cookies and stores nothing in your browser, records no screen, and never receives your name, groups or timetable. We remember your answer for 6 months in the ow_consent cookie; you can change it below.

Legal basis: the server-side counts are our legitimate interest in keeping the app running and improving it (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). Browser analytics runs only with your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), which you can withdraw at any time; that doesn't affect what was collected before.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.intro: We only use cookies the app needs to work and to remember your choices. None of them are for advertising or tracking.
items: Your groups and first name, encrypted. Until you sign out, at most 400 days.
Protects the sign-in through USOS. 15 minutes.
Language and theme, if you change them. 1 year.
Browser storage, not a cookie: whether to show every day of the week. Until you clear your browser data.

recipients.title: Who else handles data
body: Cloudflare (Cloudflare, Inc.) passes all traffic to our server and protects it from attacks, so it sees your IP address and the data sent. It operates worldwide, including outside the EU; transfers rely on standard contractual clauses and the EU–US Data Privacy Framework.
The hosting company that runs our server has technical access to it.
PostHog (EU servers) receives the server-side counts and, only with your consent, the browser analytics.
All three process data on our behalf. We don't sell or share data with anyone else.

retention.title: How long
items: Cookies: as listed above. Signing out deletes the cookie with your groups and first name right away.
Public group timetables and lecturer names: in the server's memory for at most 14 days, never on disk; gone at every restart.
Analytics data in PostHog: at least a year, because that's what PostHog guarantees and a shorter period can't be set. It contains no name, groups or timetable.
Cloudflare: according to its own privacy policy.

rights.title: Your rights
body: You have the right to access, correct, delete and port your data, to restrict its processing, to object to processing based on legitimate interest, and to withdraw your consent to analytics.

You can exercise most of these yourself: everything we know about you is in the cookie in your browser, and signing out deletes it. You can turn analytics off above. We can't link analytics data to a particular person, so we can't look it up or delete it on request.
You can also lodge a complaint with the Polish data protection authority, the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (ul. Stawki 2, 00-193 Warsaw, uodo.gov.pl).
We make no automated decisions about you and don't profile you.

privacy.outro: No ads, no third-party fonts. The code is open — you can verify every sentence on this page.

consent.text: Can we measure how you use the app (page views, calendar clicks, errors, speed)? PostHog does this on EU servers, without cookies, and never sees your name, groups or timetable.
consent.on: Analytics in your browser is on.
consent.off: Analytics in your browser is off.
